**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 of the agreement already delivers the ASSIGN preferred position in every respect:

| Preferred element | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Customer assignment to affiliate/successor without consent | § 24.1 (p0092), with "Affiliate" properly defined at § 1.1 |
| Vendor may not assign without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) | § 24.2 (p0093) — also captures delegation of material performance and transfer by change of control |
| Never to a Customer competitor | § 24.2 — "Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent" |
| No Vendor termination right on our change of control | § 24.4 (p0095) — also blocks suspension, repricing, Fee acceleration and service reduction |

Two points I checked specifically per the planner note:

- **§ 24.3 residual consent does not undercut § 24.1.** It is scoped by the opening words "For other assignments," so the mutual consent requirement operates only outside the § 24.1 carve-out. The "void" language likewise attaches only to assignments contrary to the Section as a whole, not to permitted affiliate/successor transfers.
- **§ 13.3 licence transfer aligns.** It expressly permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor "in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24," so the licence follows the assignment rather than stranding it.

A document-wide search for "change of control" and "assign" surfaced no deemed-assignment trigger, no re-pricing hook, and no other Vendor exit right. The only adjacent termination right is § 9.2, a mutual insolvency clause that expressly carves out lawful reorganizations that do not impair performance — so it cannot be repurposed as a change-of-control exit against us.
